subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: Should OpenClaw accept this scoped Codex native PreToolUse delivery path, and under what runtime/compatibility conditions may it merge?
rationale: The patch changes a tool-execution security boundary and session continuity behavior, and the required Codex runtime behavior is now entangled with a stale branch and current-main dependency drift.

options.title: Require Rebase, Normalization, And Proof
options.body: Keep this PR open but require a current-main rebase, code_mode_exec-or-current-equivalent policy normalization, and fresh proof against the accepted Codex runtime before merge.

options.title: Accept Scoped Runtime Tradeoff
options.body: Maintainers may explicitly accept unified-exec routing and fresh-thread behavior for policy-active Codex turns once the required Codex runtime is pinned or otherwise proven.

options.title: Choose A Different Canonical PR
options.body: Pause or close this PR only after another related PR is clean, proof-positive, and clearly chosen as the canonical landing path.

recommendation.title: Require Rebase, Normalization, And Proof
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but require a current-main rebase, code_mode_exec-or-current-equivalent policy normalization, and fresh proof against the accepted Codex runtime before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the prior code-mode hook contract and carried adjacent native hook relay fixups, so they are the best available owner for the security/compatibility decision.
